purpose: Source-validated correspondence inventory; not an assertion that machine checking or human correspondence review has passed.

machine_evidence.status: consult record.json; not asserted by this inventory
machine_evidence.source_versions: Exact manuscript, companion, shared-module, metadata, and dependency versions are identified by record.json; hashes are not duplicated here.
machine_evidence.inventory_scope: Public named project definitions and theorems in the listed modules. The environment-wide axiom audit also covers generated and private declarations; its count can exceed this inventory.

human_correspondence_review.scope: The prose and Lean source versions identified in the sibling record.json.
human_correspondence_review.approval_rule: Only Steven can approve mathematical correspondence; statement or definition changes reopen affected review.

ai_correspondence_checks.scope: Actual finite-rank range trace, unrestricted spectral input T, operator bounds, representative bridges, and Lebesgue diagonal counterexample.
ai_correspondence_checks.result: No weakening or assumed target identity identified in this cross-check; this is not human approval.

ai_correspondence_checks.scope: Actual L∞ multiplication, L² operators, orthogonal projection, actual compressed endomorphism trace, relative product integrability and inner-product convention.
ai_correspondence_checks.result: No surrogate operator, trace definition equated to its target, or hidden conclusion assumption identified in this cross-check; this is not human approval.

coverage_policy: Every LaTeX label in the three current section texts is represented below.
Unlabelled examples and narrative claims attach to an existing nearby semantic label; no new manuscript labels have been invented.
Definitions, notation, interpretation, claimed results, and supporting narrative calculations are distinguished.
An entry records the exact local declaration coverage and any proof-route or scope distinction; it does not assert a line-by-line transcription of every intermediate estimate in the prose.
The public declaration inventory includes reusable intermediate helpers even when they have no independent manuscript label.

source_name_validation.method: Matched every named declaration to its current namespace and declaration header in a listed Lean source; verified that all labels in the three texts are mapped and that all scratch declaration inventories are included.
source_name_validation.limitations: Source-name validation is not Lean type checking, an axiom audit, or human semantic review.

entries.label: a-quantity-seen-in-two-ways
entries.claim: The matrix [[2,1],[1,2]] has trace 4 and the two displayed nonzero eigenvectors with eigenvalues 3 and 1.
entries.scope_note: The geometric-side/spectral-side terminology is exposition, not a separate theorem.

entries.label: linear-algebra.transpose
entries.claim: The displayed column vectors use ordinary transpose, with no complex conjugation.
entries.scope_note: Lean represents column vectors as functions Fin n → ℂ. There is no separate project definition of the manuscript transpose typography.

entries.label: linear-algebra.trace-eigenvalue-sum
entries.claim: For every size including zero, trace equals the sum of characteristic roots with algebraic multiplicity; there are n roots and a root corresponds to a nonzero eigenvector.
entries.correspondence_note: Roots are a multiset. The Mathlib characteristic-polynomial theorem follows the coefficient-comparison route; no diagonalizability hypothesis is introduced.

entries.label: definition-the-trace
entries.claim: Matrix trace is the diagonal sum, including the empty sum, and is additive, homogeneous, and n on the identity.

entries.label: definition-the-trace
entries.claim: The displayed 1×2 and 2×1 matrices have products [[11]] and [[3,6],[4,8]], both with trace 11.
entries.anchor_relation: This example follows the trace definition and precedes the cyclicity proposition; the manuscript gives it no separate label.

entries.label: linear-algebra.trace-cyclic
entries.claim: Trace(AB)=Trace(BA) for compatible rectangular complex matrices, allowing empty dimensions.

entries.label: linear-algebra.trace-similarity
entries.claim: Trace(S⁻¹AS)=Trace(A) for invertible S.
entries.correspondence_note: The companion uses IsUnit S and the actual Mathlib matrix inverse; the shared unit-valued formulation is also available.

entries.label: linear-algebra.endomorphism-trace
entries.claim: The actual linear-map trace agrees with the trace of the matrix in any finite basis, and does not depend on that basis.

entries.label: check-the-statement-on-examples
entries.claim: The Jordan matrix [[2,1],[0,2]] has characteristic polynomial (t−2)², roots {2,2}, trace 4, a one-dimensional eigenspace, only eigenvalue 2, and no eigenbasis.
entries.scope_note: The alternative proof for a diagonalizable matrix is explanatory; the general trace theorem has no diagonalizability assumption and is already covered.

entries.label: finite-kernel-model
entries.claim: The ambient space is the actual complex L² space; the book inner product is linear in its first argument and equals the stated integral.
entries.correspondence_note: bookInner reverses Mathlib inner-product arguments. The finite-sum theorems hold for arbitrary measures, hence specialize to the manuscript sigma-finite setting. The ambient L² space is not assumed finite-dimensional.

entries.label: finite-orthonormal-coefficients
entries.claim: Unique orthogonal remainder and coefficients; spectral expansion; the displayed sum-of-eigenvalue-norms bound.
entries.correspondence_note: The input T is only a linear map with the stated eigenvector and zero-on-orthogonal-complement hypotheses. Its boundedness is a consequence, not a hypothesis.

entries.label: finite-spectral-kernel
entries.kind: definition and subsequent kernel and trace calculations
entries.claim: The specified spectral kernel is integrable against L² inputs, represents T almost everywhere, and has diagonal integral equal to the finite-rank trace and the eigenvalue sum.
entries.correspondence_note: The canonical L² representatives are used first. General finite-kernel representative bridges apply to a diagonal coefficient matrix to obtain any chosen representatives.

entries.label: finite-kernel-trace-definition
entries.claim: The finite-rank trace agrees with the trace on every finite-dimensional supporting space, independently of that space.
entries.correspondence_note: The canonical definition takes the actual range; equality with supported restrictions uses cyclicity between finite-dimensional spaces rather than the prose common-containing-space zero-block argument. Only range containment is needed for this stronger comparison theorem.

entries.label: finite-kernel-rank-one-example
entries.claim: For u(x)=√3 x on [0,1], the actual L² norm is 1, T has the prescribed eigenvector and zero-orthogonal action, the chosen kernel is 3αxy, the operator has the displayed integral formula, and both trace calculations give α.
entries.correspondence_note: The interval is represented by Lebesgue measure on ℝ restricted to Icc 0 1; equality of representatives is explicit.

entries.label: finite-kernel-operator
entries.claim: Actual bounded finite matrix operator and specified kernel; integral action almost everywhere; sum-of-entry-norms bound; image in the span; zero action on its orthogonal complement; basis action and matrix A.

entries.label: finite-kernel-operator
entries.claim: Point indicators form an orthonormal basis of the actual counting-measure L² space; the kernel entries are Aij and its integral action is matrix-vector multiplication.
entries.anchor_relation: The paragraph follows the general finite-kernel definition; it has no separate manuscript label.

entries.label: finite-kernel-trace-identity
entries.claim: The specified diagonal is integrable and its integral equals the actual finite-rank trace and the characteristic-root sum with algebraic multiplicity.
entries.correspondence_note: A.charpoly.roots is a multiset, including repeated roots; no diagonalizability is assumed.

entries.label: finite-kernel-trace-identity
entries.claim: A=I gives the actual orthogonal projection onto the finite span and trace N.

entries.label: kernel-diagonal-representatives
entries.claim: Changing the one-variable representatives preserves both kernel product-a.e. equality and diagonal base-a.e. equality. Arbitrary product-a.e. kernel changes preserve row-integral operators a.e. but need not preserve the diagonal integral.
entries.correspondence_note: The zero kernel and diagonal indicator are actual functions on the Lebesgue interval, with diagonal integrals 0 and 1. No diagonal conclusion is inferred from product-a.e. equality.

entries.label: three-finite-kernel-constructions
entries.claim: Ordinary diagonal integration, relative pairing, and weighted diagonal integration use the same finite kernel.
entries.scope_note: The introductory statement of linearity in the kernel is not exported as a separate project theorem; the actual integrals and the finite coefficient formulas are formalized.

entries.label: ordinary-finite-trace
entries.claim: The actual diagonal integral equals Matrix.trace A, and a diagonal coefficient matrix gives the eigenvalue sum.

entries.label: relative-finite-pairing
entries.claim: A period is the book inner product and its integral; the relative pairing is the actual iterated integral with q as input and conjugate p as output test.

entries.label: finite-relative-kernel-identity
entries.claim: The relative integrand is integrable on the product measure, and the iterated integral equals both the actual operator coefficient and the conjugated-period sum.
entries.correspondence_note: The result holds for any finite L² family, hence for the orthonormal family in the prose. Sigma-finiteness is retained for the iterated-integral identities. The final operator equality expands the continuous linear map rather than substituting its a.e. representation.
entries.proof_detail_scope: Absolute convergence is proved using Mathlib L² product integrability, product integrability, and Fubini. The prose quantitative L¹ estimate with constant (sum |aij|)||p||||q|| is not separately exported as a project theorem.

entries.label: finite-relative-diagonal-identity
entries.claim: For an actual diagonal matrix the relative sum reduces to λj Pp(uj) conjugate(Pq(uj)).

entries.label: weighted-finite-trace
entries.claim: The weight is an actual L∞ class, multiplication defines a bounded operator on actual L², and the specified weighted diagonal is integrable.
entries.proof_detail_scope: The actual Mathlib Hölder multiplication map supplies boundedness and its a.e. representative formula. The displayed sharp norm estimate is not a separately exported project theorem.

entries.label: finite-weighted-kernel-identity
entries.claim: The actual weighted diagonal integral equals LinearMap.trace of the actual compression P Mw TA restricted to V, and equals the displayed finite coefficient-integral sum.
entries.correspondence_note: P is Mathlib orthogonalProjection and the trace is actual LinearMap.trace. The span basis and its inner-product coordinates identify the diagonal coefficients; no conclusion is assumed or used as a definition.

entries.label: finite-weighted-diagonal-identity
entries.claim: A diagonal matrix gives the sum of λj times the integral of w|uj|².
entries.correspondence_note: The final theorem uses the pointwise complex modulus squared. The finite integral statement is stronger than the prose: arbitrary finite L² families and no sigma-finiteness assumption.

entries.label: finite-trace-information-examples
entries.claim: Anchor for the two-point worked example immediately following.

entries.label: finite-three-measurements-example
entries.claim: With actual counting measure, the point indicators span L², P is identity, both ordinary values are 3, relative values are 0 and 1, and both weighted values are w1+2w2, with singleton values 1 and 2.
entries.correspondence_note: Lean Fin 2 uses indices 0 and 1 for manuscript points 1 and 2. Both matrix-vector outputs and weighted matrix products are proved, with bridges to actual counting-measure integrals. The general same-diagonal theorem covers the claim that no diagonal weight distinguishes A and B.
